chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said: Our father narrated to us from Abu al-Mughirah, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying:
Whoever recites, after the Morning and Maghrib prayers, before folding his legs or speaking to anyone,
Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and his progeny. Allah will fulfill for him one hundred wishes, seventy in the world and thirty in the hereafter.

He said: I asked, 'What is the meaning of the salutation of Allah, the angels, and the believers?' He said: 'The salutation of Allah is mercy from Allah, and the salutation of the angels is purification from them for him, and the salutation of the believers is supplication from them for him.'

And whoever includes the Family of Muhammad in the blessing upon the Prophet and his family, saying: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad among the first ones, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad among the last ones, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad among the highest assembly, and send blessings upon Muhammad and the Family of Muhammad among the messengers.
O Allah, grant Muhammad the Means (al-Wasilah), the Honor, the Excellence, and the High Rank.

O Allah, indeed I have believed in Muhammad but have not seen him, so do not deprive me of seeing him on the Day of Resurrection, and grant me his companionship, and cause me to die upon his religion, and give me to drink from his Basin a drink that is satisfying, pleasing, and delightful, so that I may never thirst after it again. Indeed, You are Able over all things.
O Allah, just as I believed in Muhammad (peace be upon him) and did not see him, so make his face known to me in the Gardens.
O Allah, convey to the spirit of Muhammad from me much greeting and peace.

For indeed, whoever sends blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him) with this blessing, his sins will be demolished, his errors erased, his joy will persist, his supplication will be answered, his hope will be granted, his provision will be expanded for him, and he will be aided against his enemy. And it will be for him a cause of all kinds of good, and he will be made among the companions of his Prophet in the Highest Gardens. He should recite them three times in the morning and three times in the evening.

key_terms.الصَّلَاهُ: Blessing/Salutation (specifically in the context of divine favor)
key_terms.الْوَسِیلَهَ: The Means (a high rank in Paradise)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward and meaning of reciting the specific salutation after Morning and Maghrib prayers according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical dimensions of the salutation formula, defining Allah’s *Salah* as mercy, the angels’ as purification, and the believers’ as supplication, thereby grounding the practice in Shia theological distinctiveness. This specific dhikr, recited thrice after Morning and Maghrib prayers before engaging with others, is promised to erase sins and fulfill seventy worldly and thirty otherworldly needs, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt. The detailed invocation seeks not only spiritual purification but also tangible blessings such as increased sustenance and victory over enemies, linking devotional practice with cosmic and material well-being.
